title: Start with the complete pathway
narration:
A patient’s story. A community’s evidence. A practical next step.

PathwayAI brings them together.

I’m Yuwei Zhang from Team GreenAcorn. My background in pathology and work at NIH and CMS connect clinical evidence with policy.

Our purpose is simple: make the hidden patient journey visible—and actionable.

title: Plan before going outdoors
navigation: Plan time outdoors → Your outdoor plan
narration: The pathway starts before illness. Choose where and when you will be outdoors, and what you plan to do. Prevention belongs here.

title: Prepare, check, and respond
navigation: Learn & Prevent → Generate My Outdoor Tick-Prevention Plan
narration: Prepare suitable clothing and an EPA-registered repellent, following product instructions. After outdoor activities, check your body, clothes, gear, and pets. Shower within two hours. These precautions support risk reduction; they do not guarantee protection.

title: After a tick bite
navigation: After a tick bite → Remove → Record → Seek advice
narration: If a tick is attached, use fine-tipped tweezers, grasp close to the skin, and pull upward steadily. Record when and where it happened. Seek medical advice promptly when appropriate, including after some high-risk bites. Do not wait for symptoms if you need prevention advice.

title: Record when and where
navigation: Prepare for care → Tick encounter details
narration: Keep the date and possible exposure location in your record. That place may differ from where you live or need care.

title: Tell the story once
navigation: Prepare for care → Tell us what happened → Organize My Story
narration: Now, a fictional person feels tired after an outdoor walk and wants help preparing for care. They enter a short story, including payments, missed work, and unpaid help. PathwayAI organizes the details for them to check, change, and download.

title: Prepare questions about testing
navigation: Care & Support → Lyme tests → Before the test
narration: The testing guide helps people prepare questions about symptoms, timing, the complete report, and costs. It supports a conversation with a clinician; it does not diagnose.

title: Include daily life and caregiver experience
navigation: Care & Support → Daily life and caregiver experience
narration: Some people need help reporting. Caregiver observations, the person’s daily-life difficulties, and the caregiver’s own experience can be recorded separately. Partial answers are welcome.

title: Review payments, work and unpaid help
navigation: Care & Support → Review and download your visit and burden card
narration: Here, the fictional person paid one hundred eighty dollars for care and forty-five dollars for travel: two hundred twenty-five dollars altogether. Three missed workdays and eight hours of unpaid help stay separate. Unknown answers stay unknown.

title: Prepare a request for support
navigation: Care & Support → Choose the help you need → Getting to care
narration: A record becomes more useful when it supports a next step. Here, someone can prepare a request for transport help, asking about eligibility, cost, booking, and a return trip.

title: Prepare for a benefits conversation
navigation: Care & Support → Prepare for a benefits conversation
narration: Benefits preparation helps people organize questions and relevant records for food assistance or disability support. The agency determines eligibility. Nothing is submitted automatically.

title: Compare county evidence
navigation: Community Burden & Action → Compare Dutchess and Orange
narration: Now we move to community evidence. We compare Dutchess and Orange counties using New York reports, federal CDC, Census and HRSA context, and published research. Source years and limits remain visible.

title: Explore a cost illustration
navigation: Community → Estimated community cost: Dutchess and Orange
narration: The two-county cost illustration is about four point one million dollars in twenty sixteen dollars. It multiplies reported cases by a study mean. It is not measured county spending.

title: Connect needs with possible actions
narration: The next question is practical: what support should a community explore? Patients, caregivers, and willing partners could review transport barriers, agree on a feasible response, and track rides, appointments, and needs still unmet.

title: Summarize comparable reports
navigation: Community → See how comparable patient reports could be summarized
narration: These six records are invented. Five have usable answers; one leaves fields unknown. They show how comparable reports could be summarized, not what everyone in the county experiences.

title: Ask about the public evidence
navigation: Community → Ask AI about the public evidence
narration:
Optional AI explains a curated public evidence summary without receiving private patient cards. Story AI requires permission; the local organizer works without it.

AI can organize information, but people review its meaning. Data can reveal patterns, but it cannot replace lived experience.

title: Patients and people remain at the center
narration:
Models can explore possibilities, but people remain responsible for decisions. The patient remains at the center.

To the patients, caregivers, advocates, and experts who shared experiences and guidance: thank you. You helped shape PathwayAI.

Making the Hidden Patient Journey Visible—and Actionable.

Thank you for helping make it possible.
